section_1.title: Prerequisite: Projective Intuition
section_1.content: Briefly establish the geometric meaning of a dot product: the projection of one vector onto another. Visualize a light source casting a shadow of vector A onto vector B.
section_1.example: A flashlight shining on a stick (vector A) resting on the ground (vector B), creating a shadow length.

section_2.title: Defining the Dot Product as a Linear Map
section_2.content: Shift the perspective from 'multiplying two vectors' to 'a function that takes a vector and returns a scalar'. Introduce the dot product with a fixed vector 'w' as a linear transformation f(v) = w · v.
section_2.example: A sensor (vector w) sweeping across a field; the dot product tells us the 'intensity' of data detected at any point v.

section_3.title: The Core Concept: Duality
section_3.content: Explain duality: Every vector space has an associated dual space of linear functionals. The dot product acts as the bridge, showing that every 'operation' (linear functional) can be represented by a 'state' (a vector).
section_3.example: A robot (vector w) is defined by its sensing capabilities. The dual perspective treats the robot not as an object, but as a 'detector' that evaluates its environment.

section_4.title: Visualizing Duality via Level Sets
section_4.content: Show that the dot product w · v = c represents a plane (or line) perpendicular to w. The 'vector' w determines the orientation of these planes—this is the geometric essence of the dual space.
section_4.example: Imagine a flock of birds flying. The 'dual vector' represents the direction of the wind force; the level sets are the imaginary boundaries where the wind pressure is constant.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Recap: Vectors are points; dual vectors are 'measuring devices'. The dot product is the bridge that allows us to translate between geometry and function.
section_5.example: In computer graphics: A surface normal (vector) and the lighting function (dual) interact via the dot product to determine shading intensity on a character's face.

lecture_lines: Dot product is a linear map.
It returns a scalar from two vectors.
A fixed vector w defines this function.

section_3.title: The Core Concept: Duality
